covered: Focus and hypocentre, epicentre, fault plane and focal depth; elastic-rebound theory and the 1906 San Francisco fence-line surveys.

Seismic waves: P, S, Love and Rayleigh; the S-wave and P-wave shadow zones as evidence for the liquid outer core (callback to the interior lesson); the seismograph and epicentre location from the P–S time gap.
Magnitude versus intensity; the Richter scale and its saturation; moment magnitude (Mw); Modified Mercalli and MSK intensity; site amplification (Ahmedabad 2001, Kathmandu 2015).

Depth classification — shallow (0–70 km), intermediate (70–300 km), deep (300–700 km); the Wadati–Benioff zone and why the Himalaya produces only shallow quakes; global distribution and the Ring of Fire.
Tsunami generation — vertical sea-floor displacement, long wavelength, jet speed in deep water, shoaling at the coast; the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami and the INCOIS warning centre at Hyderabad.
India's seismic zones II–V (BIS IS 1893, based on MSK intensity), the central seismic gap, and the case studies of Latur 1993, Bhuj 2001 and Nepal 2015.
lastHandoff.next: Volcanoes: Mountains That Breathe — magma, lava, viscosity and gas content; shield, composite and cinder-cone volcanoes; calderas and fissure eruptions; pyroclastic flows and lahars; the Ring of Fire; hotspot volcanism (Hawaii, Yellowstone); volcanic landforms and soils; India's volcanic legacy (Deccan Traps, Barren Island); volcanic hazards and benefits.
lastHandoff.notes: The 'plate-boundaries' figure from Lesson 6 was reused verbally throughout the depth section — once for the Benioff zone and once for the depth of quakes at each margin — and the new 'india-seismic-zones' figure should in turn be reused in the volcano lesson (Barren Island sits on the Andaman arc, which is Zone V) and for any disaster-management or hazard-mapping question. 'eq-fault-block' is the master earthquake figure and pairs with the older 'plate-boundaries' diagram; 'tsunami-generation' can be reused for coastal hazards, for the 2004 case study, and for oceanography. The 'magnetic-striping' and 'earth-interior' figures from Lessons 5–6 pair naturally with the shadow-zone paragraph if that material is ever revised. The women-in-science thread (Inge Lehmann → Marie Tharp) was NOT extended here; Lehmann's shadow-zone work is the obvious next link and can be paid off in the volcano lesson or in a revision piece. Deliberately NOT done: the Benioff zone's role in generating arc magmas (that is the volcano lesson's opening), the later stages of the Wilson cycle, and any detailed treatment of seismic-resistant construction (IS 1893 detailing, base isolation) beyond naming the code. The 'map as argument' stance from Lesson 1 was re-established in the distribution paragraph — worth keeping alive. The Coriolis preview from Lesson 4 is still unpaid and still belongs to atmospheric circulation.
